reviewerSubstitution: The independent reviewer was Claude Fable 5.1 at high reasoning effort, substituting for GPT Astra. The ruling comment discloses the substitution. The reviewer is not the author (Claude Opus 5.5).
reviewHistory: One round on the exact merged head 5032b491 by an independent Fable 5.1 reviewer: APPROVE-WITH-NOTES with no blockers, three minors (M1-M3) and notes N1-N6 in section 8, and four surviving mutants that are coverage gaps rather than product defects (RM-E2, RM-E4, RM-E5, RM-E8; carried as CF-F1 and CF-F2); none requires a change to the head.
verdictText: **APPROVE-WITH-NOTES.** The ledger is exact and re-derivable (admission freeze before any edit; the four product leaves byte-identical to the baseline at the red commit; no test byte changed after the red commit; 11 changed files all registered, plus the reserved admission-review slot = 12 of 15; 192 of 500 counted lines recomputed `--no-renames`; only P2CG1E's own lifecycle fields in units.json; every hash in the three receipts reconciles with the blobs and the proof logs; nothing from the abandoned 526cf6d0 admission is cited as evidence). The behaviour is what the registration and my D carry-forwards asked for: both doors key on `getCampaignHostRegistry().applicationReceipts !== null` and nothing else, build their own `createDurableCampaignLaunchView()` per call and never adopt an entry's view, fail closed without a view, keep the legacy gate and the head-only answer for session-less bodies and for the absent port, answer code-only in receipt mode, and reach C's prepared create unchanged. The transport changes are reachable only after receipt mode latches on a bound transport, which no shipped caller creates. All 156 registered cases, the Task 14 selector (104), the B (45), C (54) and D (119) suites, the 35 A1/A2 suites (388), the four client callers (27) and 200 related suites (1589, 2 pre-existing skips) pass on the exact head; typecheck, lint (87 warnings / 0 errors, identical site set), format, lint:units, madge (1089 files / 176 chains, identical set), both roadmap validators, OpenSpec and the QC validator pass; 32 of 32 check runs succeed with names identical to D's list. The notes are: four of my eight mutants survived, all coverage gaps rather than product defects (the no-second-switch rule, the exactly-once terminal signal after a prior recovery, pre-ACK refusal semantics, a transient timer handle); E-DOC-1 confirmed, with the real session-bearing caller handled correctly and more narrowly than legacy; sixteen legacy route-test call sites invoke the now-async handler without `await` and pass only because the legacy branch has no await before the response. Nothing blocks merge.

reviewClassEvidence.note: The unit's five sensitive review classes, each with the reviewer's section 5 finding verbatim. None records a product defect. Authority, replay and idempotency each name one unpinned case (RM-E2, RM-E4, RM-E5) where the product already behaves correctly; they are carried as CF-F1 and CF-F2. Privacy records code-only receipt-mode refusals. Concurrency records a bounded retry and wait, with the absence of backoff noted as M2. Each verdict field is the closure's reading of the finding, not reviewer text.

authority.verdict: PASS (no defect; one coverage gap, RM-E2, carried as CF-F1)
authority.finding: **Authority.** Both doors key on the installed port alone; the view is built per call in the API graph and `revalidate` refuses any other handle or a non-transactional call (`context-mismatch`), so a foreign entry's view cannot be grafted (pinned `entryView: false`, `ownHandle: true`). No view fails closed on both doors. The receipt preflight is read-only (durable census and match census unchanged across every refusal and the accepted call) and carries no principal, exactly as the legacy gate did; the only mutating door binds the authenticated player to session membership. Residual: RM-E2 shows no case distinguishes "port installed" from "entry with a launch view exists", which coincide in every fixture; the product is right, the pin is missing (CF-F1).

privacy.verdict: PASS (no defect; code-only refusals, narrower than legacy)
privacy.finding: **Privacy.** Receipt-mode refusals are code-only: `participants-behind` loses its `participantIds`, the legacy `requiredRevision`/`behind` rows stay on the legacy branch, hydration is never serialised; the wire-string pin and RM-E7 hold this. The transport adds nothing to the wire except the non-secret remembered `lastSeq` on bound joins, which no shipped client sends.

replay.verdict: PASS (no defect; one coverage gap, RM-E4, carried as CF-F2(b))
replay.finding: **Replay.** Head-drift re-sends are the exact `sentAck` bytes (P2CA answers `duplicate`); a stale or foreign confirmation does not confirm (`appliedView` JSON equality, pinned); duplicate offers are byte-compared (unchanged); the CF7 ignore grants no confirmation and sends no ACK. Residual: the pre-ACK unknown-receipt case (RM-E4) is unpinned; the product recovers, which is the conservative answer.

idempotency.verdict: PASS (no defect; one coverage gap, RM-E5, carried as CF-F2(a))
idempotency.finding: **Idempotency.** `recover` is reached only behind `!failed` guards (message path, timer, `onclose`, `drain` call sites), the CF12 signal fires once across repeated `onclose`/`onerror` (pinned), and the confirmation timer is one-shot and nulled before it runs. Residual: a remote close after a prior recovery is unpinned (RM-E5); the product's `!failed` guard keeps it to one signal.

concurrency.verdict: PASS (no defect; bounded re-sends and wait, no backoff noted as M2)
concurrency.finding: **Concurrency.** Prepare runs before the read transaction and revalidate inside it on the same handle (order probe pinned); three injected drifts between the two are refused before materialization with censuses unchanged; the create path keeps C IMMEDIATE then M with re-admission before C (RM-E3); the transport's counter and timer belong to `sent` only, a newer pending offer neither fires nor hides the wait, and no late callback acts after close, recovery or confirmation (pinned with fake timers). DoS judgment: a server can provoke at most 4 identical ACK attempts per sent ACK (1 + 3 re-sends, no backoff, each a short P2CA transaction) and the client waits at most one 60 s window per ACK before giving up to the consumer; nothing retries on arbitrary failure. Acceptable and bounded; the absence of backoff is noted (M2).

judgments: **E-DOC-1 (confirmed).** The registered sentence "no shipped client sends sessionId" is false at the head: `missionLaunchPage.launch.ts:239` calls `resolveLaunchForces({ ..., sessionId: matchId })`, and `requestLaunchAuthority` puts `sessionId` in the POST body; `fastForwardCombatRunner.ts:366` also forwards it when a session is supplied. The dashboard facade (`CampaignDashboardPage.launch.ts`) sends no session and keeps the head-only answer. E's implementation handles the real caller correctly: the body's `sessionId` is the co-op match id, the same key the legacy cursor gate, the participant store and `materializeOwnedPlayerForces` already use; the view lists the roster by `(campaignId, sessionId)`, so a session of another campaign yields an empty roster and `gm-required` (fail closed), and a session of this campaign yields the same read-only verdict any participant would get. A client-supplied `sessionId` cannot act for another session: the preflight writes nothing, and the create door checks the authenticated player's membership of that exact session. Disclosure is narrower than legacy (code only, no participant ids, no revision rows; `activeHead` was already public on the head-only path). The client relays the body unchanged and `assertOwnedForcesCurrent` needs only `code`, `reason`, `activeHead` and `resyncAction`, all present (the 27 caller cases pass). The documentary correction belongs to the parent, as the scope and both receipts say; the "coverage gap recorded" clause of the behaviour text should go with it (CF-F5).

**Bound-join lastSeq (scope item 7).** Correct and dormant: the server reads it only on the legacy resync arm, no shipped client is bound, and a bound client's cursor claim selects nothing in receipt mode by the D/binder design. The test at `:171-233` was updated to expect `lastSeq: 99`, as the scope directed.

**Un-awaited handler calls in the legacy route tests (scope item 8).** `callSignedPreflight` (`:836`) and the six `post` users at `:374-480` still call `handler(req, res)` without `await`; only the new P2CG1E describe awaits. They pass because the legacy branches reach `res.json` synchronously (the `await` sits in the ternary's receipt arm only). This is fragile, not wrong: any later await before the response would turn those reads into `statusCode: 0`, and an async throw would become an unhandled rejection. A test-only fix; it cannot land in this PR (post-RED test edit) and is carried forward (CF-F4).

**CF-E2 (clock flake).** The causal release marker replaces both cross-process `Date.now()` comparisons; the parent writes `<marker>.released` in the `before` hook of M COMMIT / C ROLLBACK and the child reports whether it existed at lock acquisition. Sound. The author's 0-of-10 before and after on this machine, and my 0-of-4, do not reproduce the D lane's 1-in-3, which is consistent with a clock-skew cause the fix removes regardless.

**CF-E9 (lint).** The D review's "not warned today" for `campaignSyncTransport.ts` was wrong; the author measured 618 counted at baseline (warned since before E). Corrected here: 618 -> 661, same single warning; the other three leaves are not warned.

**Receipt-mode conflict wording.** In receipt mode the client's conflict card will show `Campaign launch refused (CAMPAIGN_LAUNCH_NOT_CONVERGED): participants-behind` (or `fresh-request`, `evidence-unavailable`, a precedence reason) where legacy showed a sentence with ids and revisions. Code-only is the registered decision; the wording is a client concern for whoever next opens the client leaf (CF-F8).

carryForwards.wording: **CF-F3 (consumer rejoin contract).** F consumes the `recovery-required` signal. The transport emits it twice: as the returned `CampaignAppliedResult` from `complete`/`drain`, and as an `Error` whose message is `Campaign application recovery required: <reason>` through `onError`. Reasons now: `application-refused`, `head-drift-exhausted`, `confirmation-timeout`, `socket-closed`, `send-failed`, `prefix-conflict`, `pending-overflow`, `application-failed`. Match on the typed result or the fixed prefix, not on free text; a typed error class is worth adding when the transport leaf next opens. A remote close before receipt mode latches emits no signal by design (legacy close kept), so F must own its own pre-receipt timeout, and F must not reconnect in a loop on `socket-closed` without the consumer's say (the transport never reconnects itself).

**CF-F4 (await the async handler) [next owner of campaignLaunchAuthorityRoute.test.ts].** Sixteen legacy call sites (`callSignedPreflight` at `:836` and the `post` users at `:374`, `:397`, `:423`, `:436`, `:464`, `:480`) call `handler(req, res)` without `await` and read `result` synchronously. Make them `await` (and `callSignedPreflight` async) so a future await on the legacy path cannot silently zero the status.
